subject: pharmacology
title: Broad Spectrum Agents: Valproate, Ethosuximide, Lamotrigine and Levetiracetam

steps.tx: **Valproate** refuses a single mechanism, enhancing GABA (synthesis up, degradation down), blocking sodium channels and T type calcium currents modestly, which adds up to the broadest spectrum in the cabinet: focal, generalised tonic clonic, absence, myoclonic and photosensitive epilepsies plus bipolar mania and migraine prophylaxis. That breadth made it first choice for generalised epilepsies for decades, until its teratogenicity ledger, detailed shortly, rewrote prescribing for women and girls.
steps.say: Valproate does a little of everything and treats almost every seizure type; its pregnancy ledger is the counterweight.

vis.alt: Valproate sodium channel blockade and T type calcium inhibition illustration
vis.caption: Valproate's combined sodium, T type calcium and GABA actions behind its broad seizure spectrum. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Valproate inhibits** rather than induces: it blocks lamotrigine glucuronidation (doubling its half life and rash risk unless doses are halved), raises phenobarbital and free phenytoin levels, and is itself displaced from albumin by phenytoin in a two way tangle. Its own adverse set includes weight gain, tremor, hair loss, thrombocytopenia, hyperammonaemic encephalopathy even with normal liver tests, pancreatitis, and dose related hepatotoxicity worst in children under two on polytherapy with metabolic disease.
steps.say: Valproate the inhibitor doubles lamotrigine and can poison liver and ammonia handling; know the list cold.

left.title: Valproate interactions
points: Lamotrigine levels double: halve the lamotrigine dose
Phenobarbital sedation deepened by inhibition
Free phenytoin rises while total misleads
Carbapenem antibiotics collapse valproate levels: avoid

right.title: Valproate adverse set
points: Weight gain, tremor, hair loss and thrombocytopenia
Hyperammonaemic encephalopathy with normal liver tests
Pancreatitis and dose related hepatotoxicity
Polycystic ovary associations debated, monitored

steps.tx: No antiepileptic teratogenicity exceeds **valproate**: neural tube defects in 1 to 2 percent, major malformations approaching 10 percent at higher doses, and dose dependent IQ reduction with autism spectrum increase in exposed children. Regulators therefore fence it behind pregnancy prevention programmes, specialist reviews and signed risk acknowledgements for women of childbearing potential, reserving it where alternatives genuinely fail. Preconception neurology review, not abrupt cessation (seizures endanger both lives), is the safe choreography.
steps.say: Valproate in pregnancy is the most teratogenic prescription in the cabinet; plan around it before conception.

nodes.label: Woman of childbearing potential needs antiepileptic therapy
Prefer lamotrigine or levetiracetam where efficacy allows
Valproate only with pregnancy prevention programme and review
High dose folate and specialist shared care if exposed

steps.tx: **Ethosuximide** is the narrowest drug in the cabinet and proud of it: selective T type calcium channel blockade in thalamocortical circuits abolishes the 3 per second spike wave of typical absence seizures and does essentially nothing else. It remains first choice for uncomplicated childhood absence, with valproate or lamotrigine added when tonic clonic seizures coexist. Nausea, hiccups and headache are its tolls; rare blood dyscrasias and lupus like reactions complete the list.
steps.say: Ethosuximide treats absence and only absence, by closing the thalamic T channel that paces it.

left.title: Typical absence and ethosuximide
points: 3 Hz spike wave thalamocortical rhythm
T type calcium blockade abolishes the pacemaker
First choice in pure childhood absence epilepsy
No protection against tonic clonic seizures

right.title: When absence has company
points: Tonic clonic seizures coexist: valproate covers both
Lamotrigine broader but slower to titrate
Sodium channel blockers can aggravate absence
EEG confirms the syndrome before narrowing therapy

steps.tx: **Lamotrigine** stabilises sodium channels and dampens glutamate release, covering focal and generalised seizures including absence, with a mood stabilising career in bipolar depression prevention. Its defining hazard is rash escalating to Stevens Johnson syndrome, governed by titration speed: start low, rise slowly, halve everything beside valproate, double beside inducers. It is among the preferred agents in pregnancy for its relatively favourable malformation profile, with dose surveillance as clearance climbs across gestation.
steps.say: Lamotrigine is broad, mood friendly and pregnancy preferred; titrate slowly or the skin objects.

nodes.label: Halve with valproate, double with inducers
Any rash early: stop and assess for Stevens Johnson

steps.tx: **Levetiracetam** binds synaptic vesicle protein SV2A, modulating neurotransmitter release by a mechanism still being fully mapped, and in practice behaves as the modern broad spectrum utility player: focal and generalised seizures, intravenous status second line equality, minimal interactions, renal dosing, and no level monitoring in routine care. Its adverse signature is behavioural: irritability, agitation and depression in a tenth or more of patients, occasionally therapy ending, with pyridoxine sometimes tried in mitigation.
steps.say: Levetiracetam interacts with almost nothing and irritates a noticeable minority; ask about mood at every review.

left.title: Levetiracetam conveniences
points: SV2A binding, oral and intravenous equivalence

Status epilepticus second line trial equality

right.title: Levetiracetam costs
points: Irritability, agitation and low mood in a tenth plus
Somnolence and dizziness early
Brivaracetam cousin markets cleaner behaviour
Switch rather than endure behavioural toxicity

steps.tx: **Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy** assembles the prescribing morality play: lifelong generalised epilepsy where valproate outperforms, lamotrigine can aggravate myoclonus in some, levetiracetam serves broadly, and sodium channel blockers like carbamazepine frankly worsen both myoclonus and absence. Syndrome diagnosis before drug selection is therefore not academic decoration; the wrong mechanism matched to an unrecognised syndrome manufactures seizures the clinic then chases with doses.
steps.say: Name the syndrome first: carbamazepine worsens myoclonic epilepsy that valproate or levetiracetam would calm.

left.title: Generalised epilepsy choices
points: Valproate most efficacious, teratogenicity fenced
Levetiracetam broad and interaction free
Lamotrigine covers absence, may aggravate myoclonus
Ethosuximide for absence alone

right.title: Aggravators to avoid
points: Carbamazepine and phenytoin worsen absence and myoclonus
Gabapentin and pregabalin ineffective in generalised syndromes
Vigabatrin and tiagabine aggravate absence
Syndrome misclassification is the root error

steps.tx: **Pregnancy prescribing** across the lesson resolves to a league table examinations love: lamotrigine and levetiracetam carry the lowest major malformation rates near background, carbamazepine and phenytoin sit intermediate, valproate stands alone at the top and is avoided wherever possible, and folate supplementation, monotherapy at the lowest effective dose, and level monitoring through pregnancy's clearance swings bind the whole strategy together.
steps.say: Lamotrigine and levetiracetam safest, valproate worst, folate and monotherapy for everyone in between.
